references.title: Das Holz als Bau Stoff
references.creator: Armin Hofmann
references.selection_status: individually shared reference; specific reasons and favorite ranking unstated
references.museum_credit: Gift of the Swiss Commercial Extension Office, Lausanne
references.attribution_status: Verified on the supplied MoMA collection page on 2026-09-22.
references.visual_observations: Large black angular letters interlock vertically on a warm cream field. Shared strokes, triangular counters and a diamond-shaped O make the words feel constructed from beams. A much smaller serif text block on the right contrasts with the heavy lettering; broad open areas keep the composition asymmetrical.

references.title: Der Europäische Familienzwist (The European family quarrel)
references.creator: Otl Aicher
references.attribution_status: Verified on the supplied MoMA collection page on 2026-09-22.
references.selection_status: individually shared reference; specific reasons and favorite ranking unstated
references.visual_observations: Two elongated hand silhouettes point in opposite directions across a saturated red square: a black hand enters from the upper left, and a cream hand from the lower right. Bold black lettering runs horizontally between them, with a smaller line near the bottom. Flat colors, rounded fingers and generous red space make the opposing gestures the focal point.

images.caption: Otl Aicher — Der Europäische Familienzwist (The European family quarrel) (c. 1950)

references.title: Ein Jahrhundert bittet um Frieden
references.creator: Otl Aicher
references.attribution_status: Verified on the supplied MoMA collection page on 2026-09-22.
references.selection_status: individually shared reference; specific reasons and favorite ranking unstated
references.visual_observations: A very tall, thin black outline of an open hand and arm spans a muted gray-brown field. Pale horizontal ovals and scattered small marks surround it; a smaller cream arm reaches upward from a broad triangular form at the bottom. Cream serif text crosses the arm, while the large black word FRIEDEN anchors the lower right. The narrow format emphasizes the upward reach.

images.caption: Otl Aicher — Ein Jahrhundert bittet um Frieden (c. 1950)

references.title: Album cover for the Philharmonia Orchestra performing Szymanowski violin concerto No. 1, op. 35
references.creator: Erik Nitsche

images.caption: Album cover for the Philharmonia Orchestra performing Szymanowski violin concerto No. 1, op. 35

references.museum_credit: Committee on Architecture and Design Funds
references.attribution_status: Verified directly on the MoMA collection page on 2026-09-22.
references.visual_observations: Fine concentric arcs cross rust-orange, mustard, black and gray radial sections. Some lines extend left into long parallel curves. Large black serif lettering runs through the circular center, while performer credits sit along the bottom and a compact Decca mark occupies the upper right. The square composition combines precise geometry with a muted palette.
references.preference_signals: Tentative: this individually shared cover reinforces the collection’s circular rhythm and music-related geometry, alongside Beethoven (ref-0023) and Nitsche’s Atoms for Peace (ref-0001). No specific reason for the selection or favorite ranking was stated.

references.title: Typography / Basic Principles — revised edition
references.creator: John Lewis (author; credited on cover)

images.caption: Typography / Basic Principles — revised edition
images.credit: AI-edited background-removal derivative; original attachment preserved. Fine details may differ.

references.attribution_status: Title, author, revised-edition wording and subtitle 'Influences and trends since the 19th century' transcribed from the supplied cover. Cover designer and publication date unknown; not externally verified.
references.visual_observations: A yellow book cover with oversized red-orange TYPO letterforms repeated vertically and joined by streaked, textured marks. Black GRAPHY crosses the center; smaller black sans-serif text is arranged in columns at the top. The physical cover shows wear. The frog-patterned fabric and phone interface are surrounding photo context, not part of the cover design.
references.preference_signals: Tentative interest in type as image, repetition, rough print texture and a limited bold palette; related to ref-0004, ref-0035 and ref-0046. No specific reason for selection supplied.

Designing the Modern Interior: From the Victorians to Today
images.credit: AI-edited background-removal derivative; original attachment preserved. Fine details may differ.

references.attribution_status: Title and editor credits transcribed from the supplied cover. Cover designer, photographer, pictured interior and publication date unknown; not externally verified.
references.visual_observations: A predominantly black-and-white photographic cover showing people in an architectural setting with railings, overhead linear elements and a large abstract mural of curves, ovals and contrasting planes. Pale pink uppercase title at upper left, white subtitle beneath, small editor credits along the bottom. Wooden surface and phone interface are outside the cover design.
references.preference_signals: Tentative interest in abstract art integrated into architecture and restrained typography over photography. The cover is evidence of visual interest, not proof of a preference for all interiors or eras discussed in the book.

references.attribution_status: Descriptive catalog title. Côte&Ciel and COMME des GARÇONS branding is visible on the supplied object. Exact product name, designer, date, material and authenticity unverified.
references.visual_observations: A purple rounded rectangular zip pouch or sleeve with black and pale cream circles of varied sizes. Several circles are cropped by the edges; the arrangement is irregular rather than a uniform dot grid. Small pale branding sits near the upper right. Bedding and screenshot controls are photo context, not product design.
references.preference_signals: Tentative interest in circular motifs on everyday objects, playful scale variation and a purple/black/cream palette. Connects to circular compositions in ref-0015 and ref-0018, without establishing a preference for either brand.
